title: Knock Knock, May I Come In?
theme: Knocking on the door, asking permission and privacy in the bathroom
blurb: Can needs a wee and bursts into the bathroom without knocking; his dad is in there! Dad laughs and teaches him the door rule: Knock knock, may I come in? And in the evening, guess who comes knocking?

pages.text: Can was playing ball. Bounce, bounce, bounce! Suddenly he stopped. “Uh-oh, I need a wee!” Run, Can, run!
pages.ask: What do you do when you need a wee while you're playing?

pages.text: Can burst into the bathroom without knocking. Bang! But his dad was in there. They both got a surprise: “Whoops!” Can felt a bit embarrassed. His cheeks went bright red.
pages.ask: If someone burst in while your dad was in the bathroom, how would your dad feel?

pages.text: Dad smiled. “These things happen! If the bathroom door is closed, we go knock knock and say, ‘May I come in?’ Go on, your turn!”

baba.say: These things happen! Knock knock, okay?

can.say: You got a surprise too, didn't you, Dad?

predict.q: In the evening, the door is closed again. What do you think Can will do?
predict.res: Both are fine! What matters is asking permission. Let's see.

opts.l: He calls out, “Dad, are you in there?”

pages.ask: What do we do if the door is closed? Let's go knock knock together!

pages.text: That evening, Can needed a wee again. The door was closed. Can remembered. Knock! Knock! “May I come in?” A voice came from inside: “Just a minute!” Tick tock, tick tock. “Come in, Can!”

can.say: Knock knock! May I come in?

baba.say: Come in, Can! Thank you for asking.

mech.done: Knock knock, wait, come in! The door rule is done.

pages.ask: Why did Can wait? What do you do while you wait?

pages.text: Can's turn! Can shut the door: click! He did his wee. Aaah! He flushed. Then he washed his hands. Splish splash, bubble bubble!

mech.done: Splish splash, bubble bubble, all dry!

pages.ask: How do you wash your hands after the toilet? What do you do first?

pages.text: Can was putting on his pyjamas. Knock! Knock! “Can, may I come in?” This time it was Dad asking! “Just a minute!” Ready! “Come in, Dad!” They hugged and laughed.

baba.say: Knock knock! May I come in?

can.say: Just a minute! Ready, come in, Dad!

pages.ask: Who knocks on doors at your house? Who do you say “May I come in?” to?

kazanim: HSAB.10 (unverified) · Paying attention to cleanliness and order for a healthy life: washes hands after the toilet in the order water, soap, towel; notices that closing the door in the bathroom is part of bathroom routine.
TAKB.1 · Managing the speaking process: starts a conversation at a closed door with a suitable phrase (“Knock knock, may I come in?”), waits for their turn to speak and for the other person's answer.
E2.1 Empathy (disposition): puts themselves in the place of the person inside; like Can, thinks that Dad may want to be alone in the bathroom too.
SDB2.3 Social Awareness: notices that everyone's closed door is respected at home, and that this rule applies to grown-ups too (Dad knocks on Can's door as well).
D8 Privacy and D14 Respect: says that the door is closed in the bathroom and when getting dressed, and that we ask permission before going in.
once: Show the cover and tap a table twice: “Knock knock! What could that sound be? Who might be knocking on the door?”
Ask: “Which doors do we have at home? Which one is sometimes closed?” Listen to the answers without correcting them.

Play the sounds from the story together beforehand: knock knock (door), tick tock (clock), splish splash (water), click (door shutting). Also explain the phrase “bursting in”: going in suddenly, without any warning.
sirasi: On page 2, name Can's embarrassment: “Can felt embarrassed, his cheeks went red. Dad got a surprise too. These things happen.” Then take Dad's place: “If someone burst in while you were in the bathroom, how would you feel?”
For the prediction on page 3, accept both choices: “Knocking is fine, and calling out is fine! What matters is asking permission.” Tap the table twice together.
On page 4, let the child touch Can, the clock and Dad in turn; join in with “Knock knock… tick tock… come in!”
On page 5, copy the order tap, soap, towel with hand movements; on page 6, ask “Who knocked this time?”
sonra: In the ordering game at the end of the story, put the three pictures in order; let the child tell what happened in their own words.
Ask: “Why did Dad knock on Can's door?” Give the child the chance to say for themselves that the rule is for everyone.
A game: you be the door, and the child says “Knock knock, may I come in?”; once say “Come in!”, once say “Just a minute!”, and the child waits.

Say together: “We close the door, but we don't lock it.” With a child who needs help in the toilet, ask first too: “May I help you?” That way the language of permission carries on with helping as well.

sinif.materyal: A play door made from a big cardboard box or a blanket, a sand timer or a ticking clock, a picture rule card (a hand knocking on a door, a child waiting)
adim: In the circle, remember the door rule from the story together: “Knock knock, may I come in?” Then we wait for the answer.
The children take turns to go behind the play door. The others knock twice and ask; the one inside says “Come in!” or “Just a minute!”
When someone says “Just a minute!”, wait all together, counting five “tick tocks”; praise the child who waits.
Hang the picture rule card next to the classroom toilet door; remind the children of the hand-washing order after the toilet (water, soap, towel).
In the review circle, ask: “What did you do when the door was closed? How did you feel when you heard ‘Just a minute!’?” Observe whether the children use the permission phrase and whether they wait.

evSoru: What happened when Can burst into the bathroom? How did Can feel?
What do we say if the door is closed?
Why did Dad knock on Can's door?

evEtk.d: For a week, everyone at home knocks on closed bathroom and bedroom doors and says “May I come in?” Grown-ups knock on the child's door too. Let the child draw a picture rule card (a knocking hand) and hang it on the door.

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Knock Knock, May I Come In?” Can burst in while his dad was in the bathroom; without embarrassing him, his dad taught him to knock and ask permission. In the evening, Dad knocked on Can's door too: the rule is for everyone. At home, you can model this behaviour by knocking on your child's door, asking “May I come in?” and respecting their “Just a minute!” We close the door, but we don't lock it; say this together with your child. If they need help in the toilet, ask first too: “May I help you?”
